The lateral surface area of the frustum of a solid right cone is the product of one-half the slant height ($L$) and the sum of the circumferences of the two circular faces. What is the number of square centimeters in the total surface area of the frustum shown here? Express your answer in terms of $\pi$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a right conical frustum, the upper circular face is labeled 8 cm, the lower circular face is labeled 20 cm, the middle vertical height is labeled 8 cm, and the right slanted side is labeled L. Reasoning: According to the figure, the diameters of the upper and lower circular faces can be read as 8 cm and 20 cm respectively, so the radii are 4 cm and 10 cm respectively. In the vertical cross-section, the slant height L, the vertical height 8 cm, and the radius difference 10 - 4 = 6 cm form a right triangle, so L = sqrt(8^2 + 6^2) = 10 cm. Lateral area = (1/2)(10)(8π + 20π) = 140π. The sum of the areas of the two circular bases is π(4^2) + π(10^2) = 16π + 100π = 116π. Total surface area = 140π + 116π = 256π.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a right circular frustum with top diameter 8 cm, bottom diameter 20 cm, and vertical height 8 cm. Convert diameters to radii: top radius 4 cm, bottom radius 10 cm. In a vertical cross-section, the slant height L is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with vertical leg 8 and horizontal leg 10 - 4 = 6, so L = sqrt(8^2 + 6^2) = 10. From the question text, lateral area equals one-half the slant height times the sum of the two circumferences: (1/2)(10)(8π + 20π) = 140π. Add the areas of the two circular faces: π(4^2) + π(10^2) = 16π + 100π = 116π. Total surface area is 140π + 116π = 256π.

method.method_draft: Read the picture as a frustum formed by cutting the top off a right cone: bottom diameter 20 cm, top diameter 8 cm, and frustum height 8 cm, so the radii are 10 and 4. Instead of immediately using the given frustum lateral-area formula, extend the slanted sides upward to form the original full cone. By similar triangles, the radius decreases by 6 over a height of 8, so the additional height above the top circle to the cone apex is 4 · (8/6) = 16/3. Thus the full cone height is 8 + 16/3 = 40/3. The full cone slant height is sqrt(10^2 + (40/3)^2) = 50/3, and the removed small cone slant height is sqrt(4^2 + (16/3)^2) = 20/3. The frustum lateral area is the large cone lateral area minus the small cone lateral area: π(10)(50/3) - π(4)(20/3) = 140π. Then add the top and bottom circular face areas, π(4^2) + π(10^2) = 116π, giving total surface area 256π.
